chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic framing and pastoral/application material: a homiletic sun analogy is immediately used to identify the speaker (“I”) with the light-giver and to exhort love/charity toward the elect. There is no systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping (degree structures, world-lists, metal/taste/face correspondences, etc.), and the rhetoric repeatedly reaches into institutional identity (“elect”, “my children”, exhortation).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame opener (“Once again he speaks to his disciples… in the midst of the congregation”), typical of the Kephalaia’s editorial container, not the older teaching substrate.

Didactic analogy about the sun’s rays extending/disappearing functions as a set-up for immediate application to the community/teacher rather than a self-contained cosmic-architectural mapping. Lacks the substrate’s systematic degree-correspondence style; belongs to homiletic/application discourse.

First-person self-identification (“this is also what I am like!”) and institutional/community referents (“my children… the righteous elect… believed in me”) indicate a later applicatory layer tied to Mani/community identity rather than impersonal cosmological exposition. Promise to gather the elect is soteriological/pastoral, not structural cosmology.

Direct exhortation and second-person address (“I say to you… let him love… mix with them in his charity”) with explicit elect-focused piety. This is institutional-ethical application voice, not substrate teaching.
